container.name_note: The validated versioned container name is retained; its role is now serving production. No recreation or rename was needed.

recipe.adaptation: H100 per-rank device selector baked into image; exact context-only reconciliation of upstream patches 0117 and 0119; immutable supervisor entrypoint.

observed.phase: after promotion readiness and interface/agent checks; before post-promotion benchmark suite

memory_profile.reason: Host dedicated to inference; operator requested reducing idle free HBM from 17-18 GiB to about 8-10 GiB.
memory_profile.note: Historical calibration above belongs to the previous image. Pool/reserve remain unchanged. Pre-promotion validation of the new image sampled minimum free HBM 6813 MiB on GPU 0 and 8067 MiB on GPUs 1-3 under long/mixed load; this is not guaranteed transient headroom or a four-concurrent-1M qualification. See current observed data and timestamped promotion benchmark evidence.

platform_notes: The published recipe image is linux/arm64; this host runs a locally built linux/amd64 image from the same TensorFold v0.6.0 + patches.
start.sh targets 2-3 DGX Sparks over SSH/RoCE; this host runs one container with four ranks, one GPU each, all GPUs visible for NCCL/NVLink.
The NGC image sets NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=spcx (Spectrum-X); this non-RDMA host requires NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none and NCCL_GIN_ENABLE=0.
The new image bakes the TF_GLM_DEVICE selector into the engine; the supervisor does not modify source on restart.
The old external deployment project is retained as rollback history. Its config.env and remove/recreate launch scripts are not the current deployment authority; use this profile and the GLM runbook.

rollback.restore: After approved idle/drain: set promoted container restart=no and stop it; set this old GLM container unless-stopped and start it; verify parsed health/model/context; update the production record to match rollback.

secondary_fallback.note: Separate Qwen fallback, not the primary rollback for this GLM update. Never run alongside a GLM service on these GPUs.

promotion.known_pre_promotion_timing_caveat: One matched cold 1M pair measured 186.467 s new vs 175.308 s old (+6.37% TTFT). Operator explicitly selected monitored promotion after disclosure; cause/statistical confidence not established.

profile.qualification: 17 CPU checks, bounded live chat/reasoning/tool/vision and agent/API checks, 1M retrieval, mixed 200K-prefill/4096-token decode and real restart passed before promotion. Promotion smoke/agent checks also passed. Post-promotion benchmarks are pending. Not a 4x1M concurrent, sustained-load, production-tail, workload-wide quality or gateway qualification.

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition-Monitoring Records (Records 0000000–0000017)

## 1. Scope and Data Overview

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning six asset classes — compressors (6), heat exchangers (2), condensers (3), reactors (2), pumps (1), turbines (1), and valves (1) — across 17 stations. Each record contains five measured parameters: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration velocity (mm/s RMS), and efficiency (%).

Because the dataset lacks nameplate data, design operating points, and historical baselines, this analysis is necessarily inferential. Where absolute thresholds are cited, they reference common industry practice (ISO 10816/20816 vibration zones, typical thermal-performance degradation bands). The intent is to triage the fleet, identify probable failure modes, and prescribe concrete maintenance actions with priorities.

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition Monitoring Records

## 1. Scope and Data Overview

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records (Records 0000000–0000017) covering eight asset classes: compressors, turbines, heat exchangers, reactors, scrubbers, condensers, separators, pipelines, and pumps. Each record contains five measured parameters:

- **Pressure** (kPa)
- **Temperature** (°C)
- **Flow** (m³/h)
- **Vibration** (mm/s RMS)
- **Efficiency** (%)

Because the records do not include asset-specific design baselines, this analysis uses cross-fleet comparison, ISO 10816/20816 vibration severity zones, and thermodynamic plausibility checks to identify anomalies. Where a value is unusual relative to the rest of the fleet or physically implausible for the equipment class, it is flagged for investigation.

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition-Monitoring Records (Records 0000000–0000017)

## 1. Scope and Approach

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning eight asset classes (pipeline, pump, valve, heat exchanger, compressor, condenser, separator, scrubber, reactor) across 17 stations. Each record contains five measurement channels: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration (mm/s RMS), and efficiency (%).

Because the dataset lacks nameplate data, design operating points, and historical baselines, this analysis proceeds by:

1. **Cross-asset benchmarking** — comparing each unit against the fleet-wide distribution for its asset class and against general engineering heuristics.
2. **Failure-mode reasoning** — inferring likely degradation mechanisms from symptom clusters (e.g., high vibration + low efficiency + low flow suggests mechanical degradation; high temperature + low flow suggests fouling or flow restriction).
3. **Prioritization** — ranking units by risk using a severity × likelihood framework, and assigning concrete maintenance actions with suggested intervals.

Reference thresholds used throughout (ISO 10816/20816 vibration guidance for medium machines, rigid mounting):

- **≤ 2.8 mm

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition-Monitoring Records (Records 0000000–0000017)

## 1. Scope and Method

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning six equipment classes (pumps, scrubbers, separators, reactors, condensers, turbines, compressors, valves, and one pipeline segment) across 18 stations. Each record contains five measurement channels: discharge/line pressure (kPa), process temperature (°C), volumetric flow (m³/h), casing vibration velocity (mm/s RMS, assumed), and overall efficiency (%).

Because the dataset contains no nameplate data, no baseline history, and no time stamps, this analysis proceeds by:

1. **Cross-asset benchmarking** — comparing each unit against the statistical distribution of the fleet (n=18) to flag outliers.
2. **Type-specific plausibility checks** — evaluating whether readings are physically consistent for the equipment class (e.g., a condenser at −20 °C, a compressor at 116 kPa).
3. **Failure-mode inference** — mapping anomalous measurement combinations to known degradation mechanisms.
4. **Prioritized maintenance recommendations** — ranked by risk and confidence.
